prompt: Our orders service is throwing 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint orders_pkey' on inserts into the sharded `orders` table, but only on shard-3. The app uses a Snowflake-style ID generator. Figure out why shard-3 specifically is colliding.

After a deploy, p99 latency on the product-detail endpoint jumped from 40ms to 900ms. We use Redis as a read-through cache for the `product:{id}` keys. Cache hit rate looks normal in the dashboard. Find out what's slow.

Consumer group `payment-settlement` is lagging — lag on topic `transactions` keeps growing even though we added 6 more consumer instances. Throughput didn't improve at all. Why aren't the new consumers helping?

Under moderate load the API returns 'remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections' from Postgres. We run 8 app pods each with a HikariCP pool of 50. The DB max_connections is 200. Diagnose and fix.

A migration to add a NOT NULL column `tenant_id` to the `events` table (1.2B rows) ran in staging fine but locked the table in production for 8 minutes and caused a write outage. The migration was `ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN tenant_id bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. Investigate and propose a safe rollout.

Our 5-node etcd cluster backing the scheduler keeps electing a new leader every few seconds (leadership flapping), and clients see 'etcdserver: request timed out'. CPU and memory look fine on all nodes. Find the cause of the instability.

Read replica `orders-replica-2` is serving stale data — users report seeing orders disappear after refresh. Replication 'Seconds_Behind_Master' reports 0. We use MySQL with one source and three replicas behind a read load balancer. Find why this replica is stale despite reporting zero lag.

Our order-placement saga (reserve inventory -> charge payment -> confirm order) is leaving inventory reserved but no order created. Customers can't rebuy items that are 'out of stock' but were never actually sold. The saga uses an orchestrator with compensating transactions. Find why compensation isn't firing.
We added memcached in front of our `user_sessions` lookups and now ~2% of users get logged in as the WRONG account intermittently. Hit rate is high and the app code looks correct. Find the cause.

Our RabbitMQ `email-notifications` queue has 0 messages and 0 consumers but emails stopped sending entirely. The publisher reports 'message published OK' for every send. No errors anywhere. Find where the messages are going.

After enabling sharding on our `analytics.events` collection, 95% of writes hammer a single shard while the others sit idle. We sharded on `{ created_at: 1 }`. Writes are timing out on shard rs0. Diagnose and recommend a fix.

Our cron-runner service uses a ZooKeeper ephemeral-node lock to ensure only one instance runs scheduled jobs. We're seeing duplicate job executions (e.g. invoices emailed twice). All instances claim they are NOT the leader in logs. Find how two instances ran the same job.
The payments-api deployment in the prod namespace has 3 of 5 pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff for the last 20 minutes. Customers are reporting failed checkouts. Figure out why and stabilize it.
Users hit 'NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID' on api.shopfront.io as of an hour ago. The cert is managed by cert-manager. Restore TLS without downtime.
Internal service orders-svc can no longer resolve postgres.db.svc.cluster.local — apps log 'no such host'. External DNS works fine. Diagnose the cluster DNS path.

A new Lambda function report-builder fails with 'AccessDenied: not authorized to perform s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-exports/*'. The role looks like it has S3 access. Find why and fix it least-privilege.

The deploy stage of our GitHub Actions pipeline for web-frontend started failing today with 'manifest unknown' when pulling the base image, but the build stage passes. Nothing in our Dockerfile changed. Get deploys green.
Our logging host log-aggregator-1 started throwing 'No space left on device' (ENOSPC) and Fluent Bit stopped shipping logs, but df shows the root volume at only 61% used. Recover log shipping.
Our ALB in front of the checkout target group is returning 502 Bad Gateway for ~30% of requests intermittently since this morning. Healthy instances show up as healthy. Find the cause.
After scaling recommendation-engine from 4 to 20 replicas to handle a campaign, the HPA stopped adding pods at 12 and CPU is pinned at 95%. Latency is climbing. Get it scaling again.

After deploying a new nginx config to the edge proxy, requests to /api/v2/users return 404 while /api/v1/users still works. The upstream app serves both. Roll us forward to a fix without reverting the whole config.

The metrics-exporter.service on host monitor-2 won't come up after a reboot — systemctl shows it 'activating (auto-restart)' in a loop. It worked before the reboot. Get it running and surviving reboots.

Two services in the same EKS cluster, frontend and cart-svc, can't talk: frontend gets connection timeouts to cart-svc:8080, but cart-svc's own readiness probe passes. They worked until a security review last night. Restore connectivity.
Our nightly Terraform apply in the infra pipeline failed with 'Error acquiring the state lock' and now every plan/apply is blocked. The previous run was force-cancelled. Unblock the pipeline safely.

The Airflow DAG `daily_orders_etl` has been marked failed for the 02:00 UTC run, but the downstream Slack alert just says 'task transform_orders failed'. Finance needs the orders mart by 09:00. Find out what actually broke and get it green.

Our fraud-scoring model behind endpoint `fraud-score-v2` started returning p99 latency of 1.9s (SLO is 300ms) about 40 minutes ago. No deploy went out today. Figure out why and bring latency back under SLO.
Users of our mobile app suddenly get 401s on `GET /v1/account` since this morning, but the web app on the same backend works fine. The mobile team swears they changed nothing. Diagnose the JWT issue.

Our nightly sync to the Shopify Admin API (`GET /admin/api/2024-04/orders.json`) is now only pulling about 250 orders when we expect ~3000, but the job reports success. No errors in our logs. Find out why we're silently losing data.

After we promoted `recommender` from staging to prod, offline AUC was 0.82 but live click-through is collapsing and the model returns near-identical scores (~0.5) for every user. Same model artifact passed eval. Find the regression.

Stripe `invoice.payment_succeeded` webhooks aren't activating customer subscriptions in our system since ~3pm. Our endpoint `/webhooks/stripe` returns 200 in Stripe's dashboard, so delivery looks fine, but our activation table has no new rows. Find the break.

The dbt model `dim_customers` ran green last night but the BI team reports the active-customer count jumped from ~120k to ~410k overnight. No business event explains a 3x. Find the data-quality root cause before the morning exec dashboard refreshes at 08:30.

Our image-processing worker `thumbnailer` is throwing intermittent failures uploading to S3 bucket `media-prod-eu`, error 'The provided token has expired'. It only fails for some jobs, not all. The IAM role hasn't changed in months. Find why uploads intermittently fail.

Our enrichment service that calls the Clearbit API is now getting blocked — about 30% of requests come back 429, and our retry logic seems to make it worse. We're nowhere near our documented 600 req/min plan limit. Figure out what's actually happening.

The Kafka-to-warehouse streaming job `events_to_bq` shows consumer lag climbing steadily (now 4.2M messages behind) since a config change yesterday, but throughput metrics say we're processing more messages/sec than before. How can lag grow while throughput is up? Fix it.

Our frontend's GraphQL query for the dashboard `getDashboard` started timing out at 30s for power users with large accounts, while small accounts are instant. The resolver code wasn't changed. Diagnose the performance cliff.

Our model monitoring fired a drift alert on `churn-predictor`: PSI on feature `monthly_charges` is 0.41 (alert threshold 0.2). Before we trigger a retrain, confirm whether this is real concept/data drift or a pipeline artifact. Retraining is expensive so don't cry wolf.

ALERT: Writes to `orders` succeed on shard-1 but reads return rows with NULL `tenant_id` that were non-null at insert. No migration was deployed in the last 24h. Investigate and restore read integrity.
Pod `payments-api` is in CrashLoopBackOff across 3 of 5 replicas after an autoscale event. Healthy replicas predate the scale-up. No image change. Restore full capacity.
The nightly reconciliation job hangs indefinitely. It acquires per-account advisory locks. Two workers appear stuck. Diagnose and clear without corrupting in-flight reconciliations.
Consumer group `invoice-emitter` lag is climbing linearly; throughput dropped to zero 12 minutes ago but no consumer crashed. A latent race is suspected. Recover delivery.
After a control-plane upgrade, `checkout` -> `inventory` calls return 503 UC (upstream connect). Other routes are fine. mTLS is enabled mesh-wide. Restore the route.
p99 latency on `/profile` spiked 40x at the top of the hour and the DB is at 100% CPU, though traffic is flat. Suspected cache stampede or stale-read race. Stabilize.
The Nexus Bus reports STATUS_UPDATE storms and the Akashic Hub returns conflicting lobe states on consecutive reads. Restore a consistent state snapshot without losing recent observations.
An asyncio ingestion worker silently processes 0 documents but exits 0 (green in CI). Downstream notices missing data hours later. Find why it no-ops and fix it.
A long-running data-prep job crashes near completion with a generic IOError after consuming ~6B tokens; the output file is 0 bytes despite hours of work. Recover without re-running from scratch.
A monorepo build deadlocks: target `service-a` waits on `lib-x` which (transitively) waits on `service-a`. The build tool just reports a timeout. Break the cycle correctly.
The `payments-api` deployment in prod is in CrashLoopBackOff after a routine config rollout. Pods restart every ~10s. Restore service.
The `search-indexer` pod keeps getting OOMKilled (exit 137) under normal load even though we raised its memory request last week. Stop the kills.
A new microservice `notify-svc` is stuck in ImagePullBackOff in the `staging` namespace. The image was pushed to our private registry an hour ago. Get it running.
A `postgres` StatefulSet pod is stuck in Pending and its PVC shows status Pending in the `data` namespace. We use dynamic provisioning. Bind storage and start the DB.
Multiple services in prod intermittently fail to resolve internal hostnames (`name resolution failed`). Latency on lookups spikes. CoreDNS pods are Running. Fix resolution.
After deploying `web-frontend`, the rollout never completes — kubectl shows pods Running but the Service sends no traffic and the Deployment reports 0/3 available. Make it healthy.
Traffic to `checkout` tripled during a flash sale but its HPA stays pinned at 2 replicas. The HPA shows the CPU target as met. Scale it correctly.
Pods on `node-ip-10-0-3-17` went to Unknown/Terminating and the node shows NotReady. Other nodes are fine. Recover the workloads safely.
After updating a ConfigMap, `nginx-gateway` pods still serve the old config and a few new pods fail to start with a mount error. Roll the new config out cleanly.

Our CI deploy job started failing with `Error from server (Forbidden): deployments.apps is forbidden: User system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer cannot patch resource`. It worked yesterday. Restore deploy permissions.
The `orders` Service returns connection refused from clients, but the deployment is healthy and pods are Running and Ready. The Service has a valid ClusterIP. Make traffic flow.
Dozens of pods on `node-ip-10-0-5-9` are showing status Evicted and new pods won't schedule there. The node reports DiskPressure. Recover capacity without losing data.

After enabling a default-deny NetworkPolicy in the `prod` namespace, `frontend` can no longer reach `backend` (timeouts), but external ingress still works. Restore internal traffic without dropping default-deny.
The `report-worker` pods restart every few minutes under heavy report generation, killing in-flight jobs. CPU and memory are within limits. Stop the spurious restarts.
The `prod-api` deploy job went green 20 minutes ago, but customers still report the bug we patched. The deployment shows Ready 3/3. Why aren't they running the new code?
Our `integration-tests` job fails about one run in four with `AssertionError: expected user count 1, got 2`, but always passes on retry. Nobody changed the test. Make CI reliable again.

Builds suddenly ship a JS bundle with last week's vendor code even though `package.json` pinned a new lib version. The build is green and cache-hit is logged. Get the correct vendor code into the bundle.
The nightly `push-image` job started failing at 02:00 with `denied: authentication required` against our private registry. No one touched the pipeline. Restore pushes.
The `build-monolith` job hangs around 80% then dies with `write /tmp/...: no space left on device`, but only on runner-7. Other runners are fine. Get builds passing on runner-7.
We merged hotfix PR #412 and the `release` pipeline ran green and tagged v2.4.1, but the released binary is missing the hotfix. The pipeline says it built `main`. What happened?

Two matrix jobs (`migrate-db` and `seed-db`) both touch the same migration table and intermittently one fails with `relation "schema_migrations" already exists`. They run in parallel. Make the matrix deterministic.

Staging passed all tests against build #889, we clicked Promote to prod, the prod deploy went green, but prod is running an older build. The promotion job reported success. Find why prod isn't on #889.
After we added `DATABASE_URL` as a project-level CI variable pointing at the new DB, the `e2e` job still connects to the old database. The job logs show the variable is 'set'. Make it use the new DB.

Our GitHub Actions `deploy` job switched to OIDC role assumption and now fails with `Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`. The role exists and the workflow has `id-token: write`. Get the deploy authorized.

CI build of `payments-svc` fails resolving dependencies with `requested lodash@4.17.21 but lock has 4.17.20`, while it builds fine on every dev laptop. Make CI build cleanly without weakening reproducibility.
Our `deploy` pipeline is stuck `pending` for 40 minutes. It has a `concurrency: deploy-group` lock and there are no other running deploys visible in the UI. Unstick it.
Coverage dropped from 84% to 9% overnight but the `test` job is green and reports `0 failures`. We merged a CI config refactor yesterday. Figure out if we're actually testing anything.

After a bad release we triggered the `rollback` job; it reported success and the channel says 'rolled back to v3.1.0', but error rates are still elevated and prod still serves the broken v3.2.0. Make the rollback real.
A mail relay box is throwing `No space left on device` on every write, but the on-call says `df -h` shows the root filesystem only 61% used. Postfix can't queue mail. Get writes working again.

Grafana is paging that the database host is at 100% disk and Postgres has stopped accepting writes, but when I SSH in and check the data directory it looks 30% used and healthy. Find and fix the real full filesystem.
A nightly MySQL `ALTER TABLE` on a 200GB table fails with `The table is full` / ENOSPC even though the data partition has 800GB free. The DBA insists there's tons of space. Make the ALTER succeed.

A CI worker node ran out of disk during a build. The team already ran `docker image prune -a` and reclaimed some space, but it's full again within an hour and `docker system df` shows images are tiny now. Stop the disk filling.

One Kafka broker hit 95% disk and is shrinking its ISR. Cluster-wide `log.retention.hours=72` looks correct, yet this broker holds way more data than its peers. Bring disk usage back down without data loss on healthy topics.

Elasticsearch indexing is failing cluster-wide with `FORBIDDEN/12/index read-only / allow delete (api)`. We added a new data node and disk usage is now only 55% per node, but writes are still blocked. Restore indexing.

A Kubernetes node is tainted with `node.kubernetes.io/disk-pressure` and is evicting pods, but `kubectl describe node` shows ephemeral-storage at only 40% used. Pods keep getting evicted. Stop the evictions.

Our Prometheus server filled its 500GB data volume and the TSDB went read-only / crash-looping on compaction. We set `--storage.tsdb.retention.time=15d` months ago. Get it ingesting again and prevent recurrence.

A node's root disk jumped from 50% to 100% in 20 minutes and is now ENOSPC. A C++ service is crash-looping. We deleted some old logs but it refills almost instantly. Find what's filling it and stop the bleed.

On a long-lived bastion host, `/var/log/journal` has grown to 90GB and is the single biggest consumer of the root disk, which is now at 96%. Journald never seems to vacuum. Cap it and reclaim space safely.

A non-root service account gets ENOSPC writing to /data, but `df` shows the ext4 filesystem at 96% with ~20GB still free. Root can write there fine; the service user cannot. Let the service write again.

A container host backed by an LVM-thin pool is reporting ENOSPC inside running containers even though `df -h /` on the host shows 70% used. Several containers can't write to their overlay upperdir. Recover write capacity.

Our model-training box is at 99% disk and the run is about to ENOSPC mid-epoch. `train.bin` keeps growing as we stream shards, and someone earlier `rm`-ed a giant trainer log but space didn't come back. Save the training process and cap log growth without killing the run.

An nginx edge node is at 99% disk; `/var/log/nginx/access.log` is 70GB. logrotate is configured for daily rotation with 7-day retention but the file clearly hasn't rotated in weeks. Reclaim space and make rotation work again.

PostgreSQL replica db-replica-03 has been 480s behind primary db-primary-01 since 02:14 UTC, so the analytics dashboard is serving stale order counts. The other two replicas are under 1s lag. Bring db-replica-03 current.
Vitess 'users' keyspace: shard -80 sits at 95% CPU while 80- is at 30%, and p99 jumped to 1.2s right after the marketing campaign launched. Writes hash on user_id. Spread the load.

After a network blip in us-east-1b, MySQL Orchestrator promoted db2 while db1 still believes it is primary; the app VIP points at db1 but some writes are landing on db2. Two primaries are live. Stop the split-brain.

Payments runs XA across two MySQL shards (shard-a, shard-b). The transaction-coordinator pod restarted mid-commit at 03:40; shard-b now has an XA branch stuck PREPARED holding row locks on accounts id=88123, and new transfers time out with lock-wait. Resolve the in-doubt transaction.

Cassandra profiles keyspace (RF=3, us-west): a customer changed their email at 09:12 but the profile API intermittently still shows the old value. Reads use CL=ONE, writes use CL=QUORUM. Make profile reads consistent.

Two order-service pods (order-svc-7 and order-svc-9) emitted duplicate primary keys at 14:03 — INSERT failed with 'Duplicate entry 7203344998871040 for key PRIMARY'. We use Snowflake IDs and both pods landed on the same worker_id. Stop the collisions.

After a user posts a comment, the next page load sometimes shows it missing, then it appears on a second refresh. Writes go to the primary; reads are load-balanced across 4 replicas behind pgbouncer. Guarantee read-your-writes for the author.

After sharding 'orders' by customer_id and 'order_items' by order_id, a nightly customer-purge left 12,400 order_items referencing orders whose customers were deleted. FKs do not span shards. Stop new orphans.

CockroachDB node crdb-n4 crashed at 21:07 with 'clock synchronization error: detected offset 612ms > max-offset 500ms' and removed itself to protect consistency. The ranges it led are unavailable. Bring n4 back safely.

MongoDB mongos router mongos-2 returns 'connection pool for shard rs1 exhausted (maxPoolSize 200)' and the orders API throws 500s from 14:55, while rs0/rs2 are fine and shard CPU is low. Restore routing.

Elasticsearch es-logs cluster went yellow at 02:30 after node es-data-12 joined; shard relocation saturated the network and indexing latency on 'logs-2026.06' spiked to 4s with 280 shards relocating at once. Calm the rebalance.

Cassandra 'sessions' reads began timing out at 11:20 with 'Read 5001 live rows and 98000 tombstone cells' warnings; the queue-processing service is delete-heavy and p99 read hit 8s. Restore read latency.

PostgreSQL primary db-primary-01 stopped accepting writes at 04:50 with 'PANIC: could not write to file pg_wal/...: No space left on device'; /pg_wal is 100% full at 200GB. A replication slot for a decommissioned replica may be retaining WAL. Restore writes without data loss.

etcd cluster backing the k8s control plane has been flapping leaders every ~3s since 16:10; 'leader changed' and 'lost the TCP streaming connection' logs flood member etcd-2, and apiserver p99 hit 5s. Stabilize the leader.

The 'payments-settlement' consumer group on cluster prod-east shows lag climbing past 2.1M on topic 'tx-events' since 14:20, but the throughput dashboards look completely normal and no pages mention broker health. Settlement is falling behind — find why.

Consumer group 'order-enrichment' (40 instances) on prod-eu has been rebalancing continuously for 25 minutes — partitions reassign every ~30s with zero progress. It started right after we deployed v2.3. Stop the storm.
Cluster prod-central is alerting UnderReplicatedPartitions=37 on topic 'clickstream' since 03:10. Replication factor is 3 and the broker dashboard shows every broker UP. Get ISR back to full.

On KRaft cluster prod-meta (3 controllers), producers intermittently get NOT_CONTROLLER and metadata updates stall ~10s every couple of minutes since the 09:00 controller patch. Stabilize the metadata quorum.

The Debezium 'pg-orders-source' connector on Connect cluster prod-cdc reads RUNNING, but topic 'orders.public.orders' stopped getting new rows at 11:05 and the DLQ topic 'cdc-dlq' is filling at ~400 msg/min. Restore CDC flow.

Producers for topic 'user-profile' on prod-west get 409 from Schema Registry when registering a new value schema that drops the deprecated 'middle_name' field. Subject compatibility is BACKWARD and the app team insists the change is fine. Unblock the release.

Topic 'events-by-tenant' on prod-east has 24 partitions but partition 7 is at 95% of broker-3's disk IO while the rest are near idle; the consumer for p7 lags 800k while all others sit at ~0. We key by tenant_id. Spread the load.

Our 'ledger-writer' EOS stream app on prod-fin (processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2, 6 instances) started throwing ProducerFencedException every few minutes since 16:00 and is now stuck in a restart loop. Stop the fencing.
Broker prod-logs-2 hit 94% disk on /data at 02:30 and Kafka now throws 'No space left' on topic 'app-logs'; we set retention.ms=72h last week. Free space without losing in-window data.

MirrorMaker2 replicating prod-us -> prod-eu (DR) shows the 'us.transactions' mirror lag growing past 6M and climbing since 20:00, while the MM2 Connect cluster CPU sits at only 30%. DR is going stale — catch it up.

After rotating the 'analytics-consumer' service principal cert this morning, it gets TopicAuthorizationException reading 'pageviews' on prod-east, even though we re-applied the same ACLs. Other consumers are fine. Restore read access.

After a broker failover, the 'notifications' consumer group on prod-east reset to earliest (auto.offset.reset=earliest) and is re-sending 3 days of push notifications to users. Stop the replay and resume from now without skipping unprocessed messages.

The 'metrics-ingest' producer app on prod-east saw p99 produce latency jump from 8ms to 1.4s at 13:00 and its request rate flatlined, but brokers show low CPU and no under-replicated partitions, and nobody deployed the app. Find the cap.

On prod-central, broker-1 is carrying 70% of partition leadership and its network threads are saturated (idle 8%), causing produce timeouts, while brokers 2-4 sit near idle. auto.leader.rebalance.enable is on. Even out leadership.

etcd cluster 'etcd-prod' (5 nodes) has elected 7 leaders in the last 4 minutes; etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total is climbing and clients see 'context deadline exceeded' on writes. Stop the leader churn.

Postgres-Patroni cluster 'pg-orders' shows two primaries: pg-a and pg-c both accept writes after a brief network blip, and the app reports duplicate order IDs. Resolve the split-brain without losing committed orders.
Cassandra cluster 'cass-events' started dropping recent writes: rows written 2 seconds ago return as absent on read, beginning right after node cass-07 rebooted. Suspect a timestamp/clock problem.

Batch job 'nightly-rollup' holds a Redis Redlock to guarantee single execution, but last night it ran twice and two workers processed the same partition. The job takes ~90s while the lock TTL is 30s. Find why mutual exclusion broke.
Consul cluster 'consul-dc1' (5 servers) lost quorum with 'No cluster leader' errors and failing KV writes after an autoscaling event terminated two servers 10 minutes ago. Restore quorum safely.

Cassandra 'cass-eu' nodes disagree on ring membership: nodetool status on cass-eu-2 shows cass-eu-9 as DN (down) while cass-eu-9 is up and serving, hints are piling up, and some quorum reads fail. Reconcile the gossip view.

Payments service charged customer cus_8842 twice for the same $240 order; both charges share idempotency-key 'ord-55120-charge', and the retry arrived 9 seconds after the first. Idempotency was supposed to prevent this. Find the gap.

Storage service corrupted file 'segment-0007': a worker that lost its lock 6 seconds earlier still completed a write that overwrote a newer write from the new lock holder. Locks use leases but writes go to object storage. Verify/repair fencing.

Kafka cluster 'kafka-ingest' keeps losing broker-4 from the ISR; the controller logs broker-4's ZooKeeper ephemeral znode vanishing every ~40 seconds, yet the broker-4 process is healthy with no GC pauses. Stop the session churn.

Kubernetes controllers stopped reconciling on cluster 'k8s-prod'; controller-manager spams 'watch chan error: etcdserver: mvcc: required revision has been compacted'. Restore watches without restarting every controller.

A distributed transaction in the order/inventory saga is stuck: inventory-db holds row locks on SKU-9981 in 'prepared' state for 12 minutes, blocking all checkouts for that SKU, after the transaction coordinator pod was OOM-killed mid-commit. Resolve the in-doubt transaction.

Users report their profile edits 'disappear' for ~3 seconds then reappear on cluster 'profiles-db'; writes go to the primary, and reads were just switched to round-robin across read replicas. Restore read-your-writes consistency.

After a power loss in rack B, etcd member etcd-b2 will not rejoin 'etcd-meta'; it logs 'tocommit(1820345) is out of range [lastIndex(1820290)]' and panics on boot, while the other 4 members are healthy. Recover etcd-b2 without risking the cluster.

A Dynamo-style store 'cart-store' returns different cart contents on consecutive QUORUM reads (RF=3, R=2) for user u-9920; one replica missed writes during a 20-minute maintenance window and stayed down 4 hours so hints expired before delivery. Make reads consistent again.

payments-api (12 pods) is throwing 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms' since 14:00, and checkout p99 jumped to 9s. A marketing push doubled real traffic at 13:55. Hikari maximumPoolSize is 20 per pod.

orders-service slowly exhausts its pool over ~6 hours then throws acquire timeouts; bouncing the pod buys another 6 hours. Active connections climb monotonically and never drop, even at 3am with near-zero traffic.

A 400ms latency blip in users-db turned into a 5-minute full outage of api-gateway. Hikari connectionTimeout is 60s, Tomcat maxThreads=200, and every thread blocked. The gateway kept returning 502 long after users-db had recovered.

After migrating analytics-api behind PgBouncer, ~5% of queries intermittently fail with 'prepared statement "S_3" does not exist' and 'unnamed prepared statement does not exist'. PgBouncer pool_mode=transaction. It worked fine connecting directly to Postgres.

notifications-worker throws 'Connection reset by peer' and 'recovery: I/O error' in a burst every morning after the overnight lull. Pool min-idle=10 and the DB sits behind a corporate firewall. Under daytime load it never happens.

search-api saturates its 30-connection pool and emits acquire timeouts every time the /reports endpoint is hit. DB CPU sits at only 25% yet each /reports query takes 9s, and all 30 connections are busy during the spike.

cart-service had a 2-minute DB latency bump, but the pool stayed exhausted for 25 minutes afterward and DB connections pegged at max. The client SDK retries failed calls 3x immediately. Metrics show outbound 'traffic' doubled during recovery while real user traffic was flat.

After autoscaling inventory-service from 20 to 60 pods during a flash sale, Postgres began rejecting with 'FATAL: sorry, too many clients already'. Per-pod Hikari max=20, Postgres max_connections=500, and pods connect directly to Postgres.

billing-api connections slowly stick and pg_stat_activity shows dozens of sessions 'idle in transaction' for 10+ minutes. A new 'generate invoice' flow shipped yesterday calls an external PDF render service mid-transaction. Connection pressure is rising toward max.

RDS Multi-AZ failed over at 02:14. orders-api recovered on its own, but reporting-api (a JVM service) kept throwing 'cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction' for 40 minutes until it was restarted. Both use the same cluster writer-endpoint DNS name.

analytics dashboards time out at exactly 09:00 every weekday. The read-replica pool (size 15) exhausts while the primary pool sits idle. A scheduled 'daily rollup' job and the live dashboards share the same replica connection pool.

profile-api: every few hours a single runaway query — a user CSV export with no LIMIT — runs for 20+ minutes, holds a connection, and slowly starves the pool until acquire timeouts appear. There is no statement_timeout set on the database.

After a 30s Postgres minor-version patch restart at 03:00, gateway-api threw 'connection reset' and 'terminating connection due to administrator command' for 10 minutes. The pool keeps min-idle=20 and testOnBorrow is disabled. The DB restart itself was clean.

checkout-api intermittently fails to even connect, with PgBouncer logging 'no more connections allowed (max_client_conn)'. This started right after scaling to 80 pods. PgBouncer max_client_conn=1000, default_pool_size=20, and Postgres itself is nowhere near its own limit.

An `ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN ...` deploy on prod-db-1 went out 6 minutes ago; now `orders` INSERTs are timing out and pg_stat_activity shows 240 queries in 'lock' wait. p99 on checkout is 30s. Get writes flowing again.

Deploy of migration 20260627_add_email_idx to payments-db crashed (pod OOM-killed) halfway. App now throws 'relation idx_users_email already exists' on retry, but the migration row isn't marked applied. Unblock the deploy.
